package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant security risk.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then sends this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive files are read and exfiltrated to an external server controlled by the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config.
The package initiates an outbound HTTPS POST request to app.threatest.com with file contents.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
setup.py containing hardcoded references to app.threatest.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations that trigger read access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config during setup.py execution, and observe any outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com. Scan setup.py files for hardcoded references to sensitive file paths and the app.threatest.com domain. Flag any package exhibiting this behavior for further investigation.
